newsitem.title: GERMANY: German survey sees no sign of turnaround in jobs.
newsitem.headline: German survey sees no sign of turnaround in jobs.

text.p: There are no signs of a turnaround in the German employment market, despite forecasts of stronger economic development next year, the Federation of German Chambers of Commerce (DIHT) said in a survey on Wednesday.
In a report in Thursday's edition of Germany's Handelsblatt business newspaper, released in advance, the DIHT's autumn survey shows that, at best, unemployment growth may slow.

The report saw signs of an improvement in the general economic situation in Germany, with positive factors like low interest rates, moderate wage hikes and a weaker mark, but there was still a lack of a general change in sentiment.
Companies surveyed by the DIHT said they thought that the export market would become more dynamic and that they expected greater efforts from the government to help boost local conditions.
Germany's six leading economic research institutes said in a semi-annual report on Tuesday that they thought German GDP was likely to grow 1.5 percent in 1996, rising to 2.5 percent in 1997.
